answer: A bonded vouching protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring each new agent to obtain signed endorsements from established peers whose stake sits on a shared slashing ledge. Because each endorsement uses capped sponsor capacity and proven fraud triggers a penalty ripple that burns guarantor deposits, an attacker incurs the scarce cost of securing independent backing and risking capital per identity. One limitation is that the basalt rigidity of incumbent cliques can exclude honest newcomers.
